title: Finding sweep: one evidence-carrying issue per fingerprint

story.i_want_to: have loopctl turn what the chg ledger shows is wrong into GitHub issues on the repository that owns the fix
story.so_that: the delivery loop fixes it without anyone watching a dashboard

rationale: Mark, 2026-11-18: 'where's the positive feedback loop?' Epic 50 stores the signals; nothing acts on them. chg#22 S14 defines the guards; loopctl holds every machine's rows, so it fingerprints once instead of per machine.

acceptance_criteria.description: A nightly Oban cron (FindingSweepWorker) reads each tenant's ledger and review outcomes since its last run and derives findings of four kinds: selection_miss (a chg row that passed on a sha whose gate row failed; fingerprint repo + sha + the gate's failures), flaky_test (a flaky row with no quarantine; fingerprint repo + test), missing_review (a merged PR with no counted review round; fingerprint repo + PR number), stuck_change (a cursor flagged gap or stale for more than 24 hours; fingerprint source + change_id).

A finding is a row in a new tenant-scoped table chg_findings (RLS enabled) unique on (tenant_id, kind, fingerprint). A repeat sighting increments occurrences and last_seen_at on the existing row; it never creates a second row or a second issue.

Each new finding files one GitHub issue on its owning repository: selection_miss on the chg repository, flaky_test, missing_review and stuck_change on the repository the row names. The issue carries the label chg-loop, the evidence (shas, test names, PR number, timestamps) as loopctl's own values, acceptance criteria written as checks, and the closing criterion. The issue number is stored on the finding.

At most a configured number of new issues per repository per UTC day (default 5, one module attribute and an env override documented in deploy/FLY_SECRETS.md). A finding over the cap stays state queued and is filed on a later run, highest occurrences first.

A finding whose evidence sha is a commit the delivery loop itself merged (a story stage merged with that merge sha) carries loop_depth = 1 + the depth of the finding that story fixed; at depth 2 the finding is state escalated and no issue is filed.

Filing is idempotent across a crash: the finding row is written state filing before the GitHub call with an idempotency marker in the issue body; a run that finds a filing row searches the repository for that marker before filing again.

test_cases.name: a miss files one issue
preconditions: a chg pass row and a gate fail row on one sha
expected_results: one issue create call on the chg repository

test_cases.name: daily cap
preconditions: seven new findings on one repository
expected_results: five filed, two queued, highest occurrences filed first

test_cases.name: depth 2 escalates
preconditions: a miss on a merge sha of a story that fixed a depth-1 finding

test_cases.name: tenant isolation
preconditions: rows in tenants A and B
expected_results: each tenant's findings name only its own rows and repositories

technical_notes: The GitHub write goes through a behaviour (Loopctl.Delivery.IssueFiler) with a Req implementation using the tenant's GitHub credential, mocked in tests.
Reads run on HeavyRead; writes on AdminRepo per tenant, like the reconcile sweep.
